column1: # title: ENG-205 Canterbury Tales — 3 Numbers & Formulas

column2: Chaucer lived about 1340 to 1400.
A household account records an outfit given to Chaucer as a page, the first document of his life.
Chaucer was captured by the French and ransomed during the Hundred Years' War.
Chaucer's diplomatic missions to Italy brought him into contact with the works of Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio.
Chaucer served as controller of customs on wool, sheepskins and leather for the port of London.
The Canterbury Tales was perhaps first conceived, when Chaucer lived in Greenwich near the pilgrim road.
Thomas à Becket was murdered in Canterbury Cathedral, creating the shrine the pilgrims visit.
Boccaccio wrote the Decameron, the most famous medieval frame tale besides Chaucer's.
Chaucer completed Troilus and Criseyde, his longest finished poem.
William Caxton introduced printing to England and later printed The Canterbury Tales twice.
The number of pilgrims who arrive at the Tabard in a company, which the narrator then joins.
The Host's plan projects about 120 tales, two per pilgrim each way, but Chaucer finished only 22 plus the beginnings of two others.
The Host's rule that each pilgrim tells two tales on the way to Canterbury and two more on the way home.
The surviving copies of The Canterbury Tales, none from Chaucer's lifetime, which shows its popularity.
The groups of tales into which the manuscripts fall, with the General Prologue block always first and the Parson's Tale block always last.
The number of mortal battles the Knight has fought, besides three jousts at Tramissene where he always slew his foe.
The narrator's guess at the Squire's age.
The books of Aristotle the Clerk would rather have at his bed's head than rich robes or music.
The Pardoner gets more money in one day than a poor parson gets in two months.
The number of husbands the Wife has married at the church door.
The Wife's age at her first marriage, the legal age of consent for women.
The number of the Wife's pilgrimages to Jerusalem, among many other shrines.
The narrator swears the Wife's Sunday kerchiefs weighed ten pounds.
The Wife's count of her husbands: three good, rich and old, and two bad.
The Wife was forty and Jankin twenty when she fell for him at her fourth husband's funeral.
The number of pages the Wife tears from Jankin's book before he strikes her.

column1: A twelvemonth and a day (WBT line 909)
column2: The time the queen gives the knight to find what women most desire.
The number, and more, of dancing ladies who vanish, leaving the old wife.
The old wife offers to be foul, old and faithful or young, fair and a risk to his house.
